title: Private deploy bandwidth-simulation & offline-fallback acceptance
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Define deterministic acceptance criteria and an executable test matrix that validates Private/VPC deployments behave safely under constrained network conditions (low bandwidth, high latency, intermittent connectivity) and that upgrade flows have deterministic offline-fallback behavior. This ticket scopes the PRD for a repeatable validation harness and operator runbook for: (1) bandwidth-limited bootstrap, (2) staged upgrade with partial-mirror availability, and (3) air-gapped/zero-egress fallback modes. The output will be an acceptance checklist, test definitions, and a short operator runbook used by QE/SE to validate customer-specific deployments prior to GA. The focus here is operational safety (no silent data loss, verifiable artifact provenance, deterministic rollback) rather than feature work (no new networking daemons).
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: When bootstrap is run under a simulated egress cap of 128 KB/s, node bootstrap completes within configured maintenance window (default 3 hours) or emits a clear timeout/error code documented in the runbook.

AC-02: During a staged image upgrade where 30% of artifact mirrors are unavailable, the operator performs a canary against a single zone first; if checksum mismatches or missing artifacts occur, the system must automatically pause rollout and mark canary as failed within 10 minutes.

AC-03: Offline-fallback path succeeds (operator can install from pre-staged local bundle) with no external egress required; checksum and signature verification must succeed using customer KMS keys and recorded verification audit event is emitted.

AC-04: Under 250ms added network latency and 5% packet loss, RPCs required for coordinated upgrades (leader election, image handoff) must be retried transparently and overall upgrade orchestration must reach a deterministic failure or success state; partial progress must be observable in telemetry dashboards.

AC-05: Telemetry: for every bootstrap/upgrade attempt a telemetry event is emitted summarizing: bytes fetched, time to first byte, highest observed latency, number of mirror failures, and final exit code. Events must be present in the staging telemetry sink within 15 minutes of completion.
AC-06: Security: No plaintext secrets or ephemeral tokens are written to disk during offline fallback; KMS/HSM-based signatures are validated and proof artifacts are included in the audit log.

AC-07: Rollback contract: if upgrade fails the system must revert to the last known-good model version and restore KV cache pointers within the SLA window defined by the operator (default 30 minutes).

AC-08: Documentation: runbook includes explicit operator steps for: throttled bootstrap, mirror outage diagnosis, manual bundle import, and emergency air-gapped recovery; checklist must be validated in a dry-run by operations team.
test_plan: Test-1: Bandwidth throttling matrix: run bootstrap with caps [128KB/s, 512KB/s, 2MB/s] across varying image sizes (small <200MB, medium 1GB, large 6GB); record time to completion and failure modes.
Test-2: Partial-mirror outage: Simulate 1, 2, and 3 mirror failures in a 5-mirror pool during staged canary deploy; validate pause/rollback behavior and audit events.
Test-3: High-latency degradation: inject 250ms, 500ms latency and measure RPC retry behavior; ensure orchestrator reaches a terminal state and exposes status in console.
Test-4: Air-gapped offline upgrade: pre-stage signed artifact bundle on a node (no egress) and validate install + signature check + telemetry emission.
Test-5: Operatorless re-sync: simulate operator process crash during artifact fetch and validate that node-level agent can resume or fail safely with observable error codes.
Test-6: KMS rotation during upgrade: rotate keys mid-upgrade in a controlled environment to ensure signature validation paths tolerate key rotation without silent failures.
risks: Long upgrade windows on low-bandwidth sites may exceed maintenance windows and require customer coordination.
Edge-case checksum mismatches from partial downloads could require manual reconciliation if not handled by retry logic.
Telemetry ingestion delay in closed networks may make real-time operator decisions harder; runbook must include local log extraction steps.
Operatorless scenarios increase complexity for QE harness and require careful scoping to avoid shipping untestable behavior.
out_of_scope: Developing new artifact distribution protocols (we will use existing mirror + signed bundle approach).
Adding new cryptographic algorithms; we will rely on existing KMS/HSM integrations.
notes: This ticket is intentionally test-and-runbook focused; implementation-level fixes discovered during validation should be new ENG tickets.
We will reuse the existing mirror simulation harness in QE and add a lightweight bandwidth shaper container for reproducible tests.
Expect ~2 eng spikes to triage failures discovered in the first run; allocate contingency.
